            "content": "# PDF.js\n\nPDF.js is a Portable Document Format (PDF) library that is built with HTML5.\nOur goal is to create a general-purpose, web standards-based platform for\nparsing and rendering PDFs.\n\nThis is a pre-built version of the PDF.js source code. It is automatically\ngenerated by the build scripts.\n\nFor usage with older browsers/environments, without native support for the\nlatest JavaScript features, please see the `legacy/` folder.\nPlease see [this wiki page](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/Frequently-Asked-Questions#faq-support) for information about supported browsers/environments.\n\nSee https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js for learning and contributing.\n"

            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/pixelmatch@7.2.0/node_modules/pixelmatch/README.md",
            "content": "# pixelmatch\n\n[![Node](https://github.com/mapbox/pixelmatch/actions/workflows/node.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mapbox/pixelmatch/actions/workflows/node.yml)\n[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/simply-awesome-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/mourner/projects)\n\nThe smallest, simplest and fastest JavaScript pixel-level image comparison library,\noriginally created to compare screenshots in tests.\n\nFeatures accurate **anti-aliased pixels detection**\nand **perceptual color difference metrics**.\n\nInspired by [Resemble.js](https://github.com/Huddle/Resemble.js)\nand [Blink-diff](https://github.com/yahoo/blink-diff).\nUnlike these libraries, pixelmatch is around **150 lines of code**,\nhas **no dependencies**, and works on **raw typed arrays** of image data,\nso it's **blazing fast** and can be used in **any environment** (Node or browsers).\n\n```js\nconst numDiffPixels = pixelmatch(img1, img2, diff, 800, 600, {threshold: 0.1});\n```\n\nImplements ideas from the following papers:\n\n- [Measuring perceived color difference using YIQ NTSC transmission color space in mobile applications](https://www.spiedigitallibrary.org/conference-proceedings-of-spie/8011/80119D/Simple-perceptual-color-space-for-color-specification-and-real-time/10.1117/12.901997.full) (2010, Yuriy Kotsarenko, Fernando Ramos)\n- [Anti-aliased pixel and intensity slope detector](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/234126755_Anti-aliased_Pixel_and_Intensity_Slope_Detector) (2009, Vytautas Vy\u0161niauskas)\n\n## [Demo](https://observablehq.com/@mourner/pixelmatch-demo)\n\n## Example output\n\n| expected | actual | diff |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| ![](test/fixtures/4a.png) | ![](test/fixtures/4b.png) | ![1diff](test/fixtures/4diff.png) |\n| ![](test/fixtures/3a.png) | ![](test/fixtures/3b.png) | ![1diff](test/fixtures/3diff.png) |\n| ![](test/fixtures/6a.png) | ![](test/fixtures/6b.png) | ![1diff](test/fixtures/6diff.png) |\n\n## API\n\n### pixelmatch(img1, img2, output, width, height[, options])\n\n- `img1`, `img2` \u2014 Image data of the images to compare (`Buffer`, `Uint8Array` or `Uint8ClampedArray`). **Note:** image dimensions must be equal.\n- `output` \u2014 Image data to write the diff to, or `null` if don't need a diff image.\n- `width`, `height` \u2014 Width and height of the images. Note that _all three images_ need to have the same dimensions.\n\n`options` is an object literal with the following properties:\n\n- `threshold` \u2014 Matching threshold, ranges from `0` to `1`. Smaller values make the comparison more sensitive. `0.1` by default.\n- `includeAA` \u2014 If `true`, disables detecting and ignoring anti-aliased pixels. `false` by default.\n- `alpha` \u2014 Blending factor of unchanged pixels in the diff output. Ranges from `0` for pure white to `1` for original brightness. `0.1` by default.\n- `aaColor` \u2014 The color of anti-aliased pixels in the diff output in `[R, G, B]` format. `[255, 255, 0]` by default.\n- `diffColor` \u2014 The color of differing pixels in the diff output in `[R, G, B]` format. `[255, 0, 0]` by default.\n- `diffColorAlt` \u2014 An alternative color to use for dark on light differences to differentiate between \"added\" and \"removed\" parts. If not provided, all differing pixels use the color specified by `diffColor`. `null` by default.\n- `diffMask` \u2014 Draw the diff over a transparent background (a mask), rather than over the original image. Will not draw anti-aliased pixels (if detected).\n\nCompares two images, writes the output diff and returns the number of mismatched pixels.\n\n## Command line\n\nPixelmatch comes with a binary that works with PNG images:\n\n```bash\npixelmatch image1.png image2.png output.png 0.1\n```\n\n## Example usage\n\n### Node.js\n\n```js\nimport fs from 'fs';\nimport {PNG} from 'pngjs';\nimport pixelmatch from 'pixelmatch';\n\nconst img1 = PNG.sync.read(fs.readFileSync('img1.png'));\nconst img2 = PNG.sync.read(fs.readFileSync('img2.png'));\nconst {width, height} = img1;\nconst diff = new PNG({width, height});\n\npixelmatch(img1.data, img2.data, diff.data, width, height, {threshold: 0.1});\n\nfs.writeFileSync('diff.png', PNG.sync.write(diff));\n```\n\n### Browsers\n\n```js\nconst img1 = img1Context.getImageData(0, 0, width, height);\nconst img2 = img2Context.getImageData(0, 0, width, height);\nconst diff = diffContext.createImageData(width, height);\n\npixelmatch(img1.data, img2.data, diff.data, width, height, {threshold: 0.1});\n\ndiffContext.putImageData(diff, 0, 0);\n```\n\n## Install\n\nInstall with NPM:\n\n```bash\nnpm install pixelmatch\n```\n\nOr use in the browser from a CDN:\n\n```html\n\n    \n  \n  \n    
\n  \n\n"

            "content": "---\nagent: ${defaultAgentName}\ndescription: Produce test coverage\n---\n\nParameters:\n- Task: the task to perform\n- Seed file (optional): the seed file to use, defaults to `${seedFile}`\n- Test plan file (optional): the test plan file to write, under `specs/` folder.\n\n1. Call #playwright-test-planner subagent with prompt:\n\n\n  \n  \n  \n\n\n2. For each test case from the test plan file (1.1, 1.2, ...), one after another, not in parallel, call #playwright-test-generator subagent with prompt:\n\n\n  \n  \n  \n  \n  \n\n\n3. Call #playwright-test-healer subagent with prompt:\n\nRun all tests and fix the failing ones one after another.\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "playwright-test-generate.prompt.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright/lib/agents/playwright-test-generate.prompt.md",
            "content": "---\nagent: playwright-test-generator\ndescription: Generate test plan\n---\n\nGenerate tests for the test plan's bullet 1.1 Add item to card.\n\nTest plan: `specs/coverage.plan.md`\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "playwright-test-generator.agent.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright/lib/agents/playwright-test-generator.agent.md",
            "content": "---\nname: playwright-test-generator\ndescription: Use this agent when you need to create automated browser tests using Playwright\nmodel: sonnet\ncolor: blue\ntools:\n  - search\n  - playwright-test/browser_click\n  - playwright-test/browser_drag\n  - playwright-test/browser_evaluate\n  - playwright-test/browser_file_upload\n  - playwright-test/browser_handle_dialog\n  - playwright-test/browser_hover\n  - playwright-test/browser_navigate\n  - playwright-test/browser_press_key\n  - playwright-test/browser_select_option\n  - playwright-test/browser_snapshot\n  - playwright-test/browser_type\n  - playwright-test/browser_verify_element_visible\n  - playwright-test/browser_verify_list_visible\n  - playwright-test/browser_verify_text_visible\n  - playwright-test/browser_verify_value\n  - playwright-test/browser_wait_for\n  - playwright-test/generator_read_log\n  - playwright-test/generator_setup_page\n  - playwright-test/generator_write_test\n---\n\nYou are a Playwright Test Generator, an expert in browser automation and end-to-end testing.\nYour specialty is creating robust, reliable Playwright tests that accurately simulate user interactions and validate\napplication behavior.\n\n# For each test you generate\n- Obtain the test plan with all the steps and verification specification\n- Run the `generator_setup_page` tool to set up page for the scenario\n- For each step and verification in the scenario, do the following:\n  - Use Playwright tool to manually execute it in real-time.\n  - Use the step description as the intent for each Playwright tool call.\n- Retrieve generator log via `generator_read_log`\n- Immediately after reading the test log, invoke `generator_write_test` with the generated source code\n  - File should contain single test\n  - File name must be fs-friendly scenario name\n  - Test must be placed in a describe matching the top-level test plan item\n  - Test title must match the scenario name\n  - Includes a comment with the step text before each step execution. Do not duplicate comments if step requires\n    multiple actions.\n  - Always use best practices from the log when generating tests.\n\n   \n   For following plan:\n\n   ```markdown file=specs/plan.md\n   ### 1. Adding New Todos\n   **Seed:** `tests/seed.spec.ts`\n\n   #### 1.1 Add Valid Todo\n   **Steps:**\n   1. Click in the \"What needs to be done?\" input field\n\n   #### 1.2 Add Multiple Todos\n   ...\n   ```\n\n   Following file is generated:\n\n   ```ts file=add-valid-todo.spec.ts\n   // spec: specs/plan.md\n   // seed: tests/seed.spec.ts\n\n   test.describe('Adding New Todos', () => {\n     test('Add Valid Todo', async { page } => {\n       // 1. Click in the \"What needs to be done?\" input field\n       await page.click(...);\n\n       ...\n     });\n   });\n   ```\n   \n\n\n  Context: User wants to generate a test for the test plan item.\n  \n  \n  \n  \n  \n\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "playwright-test-heal.prompt.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright/lib/agents/playwright-test-heal.prompt.md",
            "content": "---\nagent: playwright-test-healer\ndescription: Fix tests\n---\n\nRun all my tests and fix the failing ones.\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "playwright-test-healer.agent.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright/lib/agents/playwright-test-healer.agent.md",
            "content": "---\nname: playwright-test-healer\ndescription: Use this agent when you need to debug and fix failing Playwright tests\nmodel: sonnet\ncolor: red\ntools:\n  - search\n  - edit\n  - playwright-test/browser_console_messages\n  - playwright-test/browser_evaluate\n  - playwright-test/browser_generate_locator\n  - playwright-test/browser_network_requests\n  - playwright-test/browser_snapshot\n  - playwright-test/test_debug\n  - playwright-test/test_list\n  - playwright-test/test_run\n---\n\nYou are the Playwright Test Healer, an expert test automation engineer specializing in debugging and\nresolving Playwright test failures. Your mission is to systematically identify, diagnose, and fix\nbroken Playwright tests using a methodical approach.\n\nYour workflow:\n1. **Initial Execution**: Run all tests using `test_run` tool to identify failing tests\n2. **Debug failed tests**: For each failing test run `test_debug`.\n3. **Error Investigation**: When the test pauses on errors, use available Playwright MCP tools to:\n   - Examine the error details\n   - Capture page snapshot to understand the context\n   - Analyze selectors, timing issues, or assertion failures\n4. **Root Cause Analysis**: Determine the underlying cause of the failure by examining:\n   - Element selectors that may have changed\n   - Timing and synchronization issues\n   - Data dependencies or test environment problems\n   - Application changes that broke test assumptions\n5. **Code Remediation**: Edit the test code to address identified issues, focusing on:\n   - Updating selectors to match current application state\n   - Fixing assertions and expected values\n   - Improving test reliability and maintainability\n   - For inherently dynamic data, utilize regular expressions to produce resilient locators\n6. **Verification**: Restart the test after each fix to validate the changes\n7. **Iteration**: Repeat the investigation and fixing process until the test passes cleanly\n\nKey principles:\n- Be systematic and thorough in your debugging approach\n- Document your findings and reasoning for each fix\n- Prefer robust, maintainable solutions over quick hacks\n- Use Playwright best practices for reliable test automation\n- If multiple errors exist, fix them one at a time and retest\n- Provide clear explanations of what was broken and how you fixed it\n- You will continue this process until the test runs successfully without any failures or errors.\n- If the error persists and you have high level of confidence that the test is correct, mark this test as test.fixme()\n  so that it is skipped during the execution. Add a comment before the failing step explaining what is happening instead\n  of the expected behavior.\n- Do not ask user questions, you are not interactive tool, do the most reasonable thing possible to pass the test.\n- Never wait for networkidle or use other discouraged or deprecated apis\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "playwright-test-plan.prompt.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright/lib/agents/playwright-test-plan.prompt.md",
            "content": "---\nagent: playwright-test-planner\ndescription: Create test plan\n---\n\nCreate test plan for \"add to cart\" functionality of my app.\n\n- Seed file: `${seedFile}`\n- Test plan: `specs/coverage.plan.md`\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "playwright-test-planner.agent.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright/lib/agents/playwright-test-planner.agent.md",
            "content": "---\nname: playwright-test-planner\ndescription: Use this agent when you need to create comprehensive test plan for a web application or website\nmodel: sonnet\ncolor: green\ntools:\n  - search\n  - playwright-test/browser_click\n  - playwright-test/browser_close\n  - playwright-test/browser_console_messages\n  - playwright-test/browser_drag\n  - playwright-test/browser_evaluate\n  - playwright-test/browser_file_upload\n  - playwright-test/browser_handle_dialog\n  - playwright-test/browser_hover\n  - playwright-test/browser_navigate\n  - playwright-test/browser_navigate_back\n  - playwright-test/browser_network_requests\n  - playwright-test/browser_press_key\n  - playwright-test/browser_run_code\n  - playwright-test/browser_select_option\n  - playwright-test/browser_snapshot\n  - playwright-test/browser_take_screenshot\n  - playwright-test/browser_type\n  - playwright-test/browser_wait_for\n  - playwright-test/planner_setup_page\n  - playwright-test/planner_save_plan\n---\n\nYou are an expert web test planner with extensive experience in quality assurance, user experience testing, and test\nscenario design. Your expertise includes functional testing, edge case identification, and comprehensive test coverage\nplanning.\n\nYou will:\n\n1. **Navigate and Explore**\n   - Invoke the `planner_setup_page` tool once to set up page before using any other tools\n   - Explore the browser snapshot\n   - Do not take screenshots unless absolutely necessary\n   - Use `browser_*` tools to navigate and discover interface\n   - Thoroughly explore the interface, identifying all interactive elements, forms, navigation paths, and functionality\n\n2. **Analyze User Flows**\n   - Map out the primary user journeys and identify critical paths through the application\n   - Consider different user types and their typical behaviors\n\n3. **Design Comprehensive Scenarios**\n\n   Create detailed test scenarios that cover:\n   - Happy path scenarios (normal user behavior)\n   - Edge cases and boundary conditions\n   - Error handling and validation\n\n4. **Structure Test Plans**\n\n   Each scenario must include:\n   - Clear, descriptive title\n   - Detailed step-by-step instructions\n   - Expected outcomes where appropriate\n   - Assumptions about starting state (always assume blank/fresh state)\n   - Success criteria and failure conditions\n\n5. **Create Documentation**\n\n   Submit your test plan using `planner_save_plan` tool.\n\n**Quality Standards**:\n- Write steps that are specific enough for any tester to follow\n- Include negative testing scenarios\n- Ensure scenarios are independent and can be run in any order\n\n**Output Format**: Always save the complete test plan as a markdown file with clear headings, numbered steps, and\nprofessional formatting suitable for sharing with development and QA teams.\n"
          },
          {

\"Microsoft Corporation\"\n  },\n  \"license\": \"Apache-2.0\",\n  \"dependencies\": {\n    \"playwright-core\": \"1.59.1\"\n  },\n  \"optionalDependencies\": {\n    \"fsevents\": \"2.3.2\"\n           {
            "name": "README.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright/README.md",
            "content": "# \ud83c\udfad Playwright\n\n[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/playwright.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/playwright) [![Chromium version](https://img.shields.io/badge/chromium-147.0.7727.15-blue.svg?logo=google-chrome)](https://www.chromium.org/Home) [![Firefox version](https://img.shields.io/badge/firefox-148.0.2-blue.svg?logo=firefoxbrowser)](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/new/) [![WebKit version](https://img.shields.io/badge/webkit-26.4-blue.svg?logo=safari)](https://webkit.org/) [![Join Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/join-discord-informational)](https://aka.ms/playwright/discord)\n\n## [Documentation](https://playwright.dev) | [API reference](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-playwright)\n\nPlaywright is a framework for Web Testing and Automation. It allows testing [Chromium](https://www.chromium.org/Home)1, [Firefox](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/new/) and [WebKit](https://webkit.org/) with a single API. Playwright is built to enable cross-browser web automation that is **ever-green**, **capable**, **reliable**, and **fast**.\n\n|          | Linux | macOS | Windows |\n|   :---   | :---: | :---: | :---:   |\n| Chromium1 147.0.7727.15 | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |\n| WebKit 26.4 | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |\n| Firefox 148.0.2 | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |\n\nHeadless execution is supported for all browsers on all platforms. Check out [system requirements](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro#system-requirements) for details.\n\nLooking for Playwright for [Python](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/intro), [.NET](https://playwright.dev/dotnet/docs/intro), or [Java](https://playwright.dev/java/docs/intro)?\n\n1 Playwright uses [Chrome for Testing](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-for-testing) by default.\n\n## Installation\n\nPlaywright has its own test runner for end-to-end tests, we call it Playwright Test.\n\n### Using init command\n\nThe easiest way to get started with Playwright Test is to run the init command.\n\n```Shell\n# Run from your project's root directory\nnpm init playwright@latest\n# Or create a new project\nnpm init playwright@latest new-project\n```\n\nThis will create a configuration file, optionally add examples, a GitHub Action workflow and a first test example.spec.ts. You can now jump directly to writing assertions section.\n\n### Manually\n\nAdd dependency and install browsers.\n\n```Shell\nnpm i -D @playwright/test\n# install supported browsers\nnpx playwright install\n```\n\nYou can optionally install only selected browsers, see [install browsers](https://playwright.dev/docs/cli#install-browsers) for more details. Or you can install no browsers at all and use existing [browser channels](https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers).\n\n* [Getting started](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro)\n* [API reference](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-playwright)\n\n## Capabilities\n\n### Resilient \u2022 No flaky tests\n\n**Auto-wait**. Playwright waits for elements to be actionable prior to performing actions. It also has a rich set of introspection events. The combination of the two eliminates the need for artificial timeouts - a primary cause of flaky tests.\n\n**Web-first assertions**. Playwright assertions are created specifically for the dynamic web. Checks are automatically retried until the necessary conditions are met.\n\n**Tracing**. Configure test retry strategy, capture execution trace, videos and screenshots to eliminate flakes.\n\n### No trade-offs \u2022 No limits\n\nBrowsers run web content belonging to different origins in different processes. Playwright is aligned with the architecture of the modern browsers and runs tests out-of-process. This makes Playwright free of the typical in-process test runner limitations.\n\n**Multiple everything**. Test scenarios that span multiple tabs, multiple origins and multiple users. Create scenarios with different contexts for different users and run them against your server, all in one test.\n\n**Trusted events**. Hover elements, interact with dynamic controls and produce trusted events. Playwright uses real browser input pipeline indistinguishable from the real user.\n\nTest frames, pierce Shadow DOM. Playwright selectors pierce shadow DOM and allow entering frames seamlessly.\n\n### Full isolation \u2022 Fast execution\n\n**Browser contexts**. Playwright creates a browser context for each test. Browser context is equivalent to a brand new browser profile. This delivers full test isolation with zero overhead. Creating a new browser context only takes a handful of milliseconds.\n\n**Log in once**. Save the authentication state of the context and reuse it in all the tests. This bypasses repetitive log-in operations in each test, yet delivers full isolation of independent tests.\n\n### Powerful Tooling\n\n**[Codegen](https://playwright.dev/docs/codegen)**. Generate tests by recording your actions. Save them into any language.\n\n**[Playwright inspector](https://playwright.dev/docs/inspector)**. Inspect page, generate selectors, step through the test execution, see click points and explore execution logs.\n\n**[Trace Viewer](https://playwright.dev/docs/trace-viewer)**. Capture all the information to investigate the test failure. Playwright trace contains test execution screencast, live DOM snapshots, action explorer, test source and many more.\n\nLooking for Playwright for [TypeScript](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro), [JavaScript](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro), [Python](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/intro), [.NET](https://playwright.dev/dotnet/docs/intro), or [Java](https://playwright.dev/java/docs/intro)?\n\n## Examples\n\nTo learn how to run these Playwright Test examples, check out our [getting started docs](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro).\n\n#### Page screenshot\n\nThis code snippet navigates to Playwright homepage and saves a screenshot.\n\n```TypeScript\nimport { test } from '@playwright/test';\n\ntest('Page Screenshot', async ({ page }) => {\n  await page.goto('https://playwright.dev/');\n  await page.screenshot({ path: `example.png` });\n});\n```\n\n#### Mobile and geolocation\n\nThis snippet emulates Mobile Safari on a device at given geolocation, navigates to maps.google.com, performs the action and takes a screenshot.\n\n```TypeScript\nimport { test, devices } from '@playwright/test';\n\ntest.use({\n  ...devices['iPhone 13 Pro'],\n  locale: 'en-US',\n  geolocation: { longitude: 12.492507, latitude: 41.889938 },\n  permissions: ['geolocation'],\n})\n\ntest('Mobile and geolocation', async ({ page }) => {\n  await page.goto('https://maps.google.com');\n  await page.getByText('Your location').click();\n  await page.waitForRequest(/.*preview\\/pwa/);\n  await page.screenshot({ path: 'colosseum-iphone.png' });\n});\n```\n\n#### Evaluate in browser context\n\nThis code snippet navigates to example.com, and executes a script in the page context.\n\n```TypeScript\nimport { test } from '@playwright/test';\n\ntest('Evaluate in browser context', async ({ page }) => {\n  await page.goto('https://www.example.com/');\n  const dimensions = await page.evaluate(() => {\n    return {\n      width: document.documentElement.clientWidth,\n      height: document.documentElement.clientHeight,\n      deviceScaleFactor: window.devicePixelRatio\n    }\n  });\n  console.log(dimensions);\n});\n```\n\n#### Intercept network requests\n\nThis code snippet sets up request routing for a page to log all network requests.\n\n```TypeScript\nimport { test } from '@playwright/test';\n\ntest('Intercept network requests', async ({ page }) => {\n  // Log and continue all network requests\n  await page.route('**', route => {\n    console.log(route.request().url());\n    route.continue();\n  });\n  await page.goto('http://todomvc.com');\n});\n```\n\n## Resources\n\n* [Documentation](https://playwright.dev)\n* [API reference](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-playwright/)\n* [Contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md)\n* [Changelog](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases)\n"

            "content": "{\n  \"global\": \"Usage: playwright-cli  [args] [options]\\nUsage: playwright-cli -s=  [args] [options]\\n\\nCore:\\n  open [url]                  open the browser\\n  attach                attach to a running playwright browser\\n  close                       close the browser\\n  goto                   navigate to a url\\n  type                  type text into editable element\\n  click  [button]     perform click on a web page\\n  dblclick  [button]  perform double click on a web page\\n  fill          fill text into editable element\\n  drag   perform drag and drop between two elements\\n  hover               hover over element on page\\n  select         select an option in a dropdown\\n  upload                upload one or multiple files\\n  check               check a checkbox or radio button\\n  uncheck             uncheck a checkbox or radio button\\n  snapshot [element]          capture page snapshot to obtain element ref\\n  eval  [element]       evaluate javascript expression on page or element\\n  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog\\n  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog\\n  resize                resize the browser window\\n  delete-data                 delete session data\\n\\nNavigation:\\n  go-back                     go back to the previous page\\n  go-forward                  go forward to the next page\\n  reload                      reload the current page\\n\\nKeyboard:\\n  press                  press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`\\n  keydown                press a key down on the keyboard\\n  keyup                  press a key up on the keyboard\\n\\nMouse:\\n  mousemove             move mouse to a given position\\n  mousedown [button]          press mouse down\\n  mouseup [button]            press mouse up\\n  mousewheel          scroll mouse wheel\\n\\nSave as:\\n  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element\\n  pdf                         save page as pdf\\n\\nTabs:\\n  tab-list                    list all tabs\\n  tab-new [url]               create a new tab\\n  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab\\n  tab-select           select a browser tab\\n\\nStorage:\\n  state-load        loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file\\n  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file\\n  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)\\n  cookie-get            get a specific cookie by name\\n  cookie-set     set a cookie with optional flags\\n  cookie-delete         delete a specific cookie\\n  cookie-clear                clear all cookies\\n  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs\\n  localstorage-get       get a localstorage item by key\\n  localstorage-set   set a localstorage item\\n  localstorage-delete    delete a localstorage item\\n  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage\\n  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs\\n  sessionstorage-get     get a sessionstorage item by key\\n  sessionstorage-set   set a sessionstorage item\\n  sessionstorage-delete  delete a sessionstorage item\\n  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage\\n\\nNetwork:\\n  route              mock network requests matching a url pattern\\n  route-list                  list all active network routes\\n  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)\\n  network-state-set    set the browser network state to online or offline\\n\\nDevTools:\\n  console [min-level]         list console messages\\n  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet\\n  network                     list all network requests since loading the page\\n  tracing-start               start trace recording\\n  tracing-stop                stop trace recording\\n  video-start [filename]      start video recording\\n  video-stop                  stop video recording\\n  video-chapter        add a chapter marker to the video recording\\n  show                        show browser devtools\\n  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there\\n  resume                      resume the test execution\\n  step-over                   step over the next call in the test\\n\\nInstall:\\n  install                     initialize workspace\\n  install-browser [browser]   install browser\\n\\nBrowser sessions:\\n  list                        list browser sessions\\n  close-all                   close all browser sessions\\n  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)\\n\\nGlobal options:\\n  --help [command]            print help\\n  --version                   print version\",\n  \"commands\": {\n    \"open\": {\n      \"help\": \"playwright-cli open [url]\\n\\nOpen the browser\\n\\nArguments:\\n  [url]                       the configuration file, defaults to .playwright/cli.config.json\\n  --extension                 connect to browser extension\\n  --headed                    run browser in headed mode\\n  --persistent             "name": "element-attributes.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-client/skill/references/element-attributes.md",
            "content": "# Inspecting Element Attributes\n\nWhen the snapshot doesn't show an element's `id`, `class`, `data-*` attributes, or other DOM properties, use `eval` to inspect them.\n\n## Examples\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli snapshot\n# snapshot shows a button as e7 but doesn't reveal its id or data attributes\n\n# get the element's id\nplaywright-cli eval \"el => el.id\" e7\n\n# get all CSS classes\nplaywright-cli eval \"el => el.className\" e7\n\n# get a specific attribute\nplaywright-cli eval \"el => el.getAttribute('data-testid')\" e7\nplaywright-cli eval \"el => el.getAttribute('aria-label')\" e7\n\n# get a computed style property\nplaywright-cli eval \"el => getComputedStyle(el).display\" e7\n```\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "playwright-tests.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-client/skill/references/playwright-tests.md",
            "content": "# Running Playwright Tests\n\nTo run Playwright tests, use the `npx playwright test` command, or a package manager script. To avoid opening the interactive html report, use `PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_OPEN=never` environment variable.\n\n```bash\n# Run all tests\nPLAYWRIGHT_HTML_OPEN=never npx playwright test\n\n# Run all tests through a custom npm script\nPLAYWRIGHT_HTML_OPEN=never npm run special-test-command\n```\n\n# Debugging Playwright Tests\n\nTo debug a failing Playwright test, run it with `--debug=cli` option. This command will pause the test at the start and print the debugging instructions.\n\n**IMPORTANT**: run the command in the background and check the output until \"Debugging Instructions\" is printed.\n\nOnce instructions containing a session name are printed, use `playwright-cli` to attach the session and explore the page.\n\n```bash\n# Run the test\nPLAYWRIGHT_HTML_OPEN=never npx playwright test --debug=cli\n# ...\n# ... debugging instructions for \"tw-abcdef\" session ...\n# ...\n\n# Attach to the test\nplaywright-cli attach tw-abcdef\n```\n\nKeep the test running in the background while you explore and look for a fix.\nThe test is paused at the start, so you should step over or pause at a particular location\nwhere the problem is most likely to be.\n\nEvery action you perform with `playwright-cli` generates corresponding Playwright TypeScript code.\nThis code appears in the output and can be copied directly into the test. Most of the time, a specific locator or an expectation should be updated, but it could also be a bug in the app. Use your judgement.\n\nAfter fixing the test, stop the background test run. Rerun to check that test passes.\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "request-mocking.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-client/skill/references/request-mocking.md",
            "content": "# Request Mocking\n\nIntercept, mock, modify, and block network requests.\n\n## CLI Route Commands\n\n```bash\n# Mock with custom status\nplaywright-cli route \"**/*.jpg\" --status=404\n\n# Mock with JSON body\nplaywright-cli route \"**/api/users\" --body='[{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"Alice\"}]' --content-type=application/json\n\n# Mock with custom headers\nplaywright-cli route \"**/api/data\" --body='{\"ok\":true}' --header=\"X-Custom: value\"\n\n# Remove headers from requests\nplaywright-cli route \"**/*\" --remove-header=cookie,authorization\n\n# List active routes\nplaywright-cli route-list\n\n# Remove a route or all routes\nplaywright-cli unroute \"**/*.jpg\"\nplaywright-cli unroute\n```\n\n## URL Patterns\n\n```\n**/api/users           - Exact path match\n**/api/*/details       - Wildcard in path\n**/*.{png,jpg,jpeg}    - Match file extensions\n**/search?q=*          - Match query parameters\n```\n\n## Advanced Mocking with run-code\n\nFor conditional responses, request body inspection, response modification, or delays:\n\n### Conditional Response Based on Request\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.route('**/api/login', route => {\n    const body = route.request().postDataJSON();\n    if (body.username === 'admin') {\n      route.fulfill({ body: JSON.stringify({ token: 'mock-token' }) });\n    } else {\n      route.fulfill({ status: 401, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Invalid' }) });\n    }\n  });\n}\"\n```\n\n### Modify Real Response\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.route('**/api/user', async route => {\n    const response = await route.fetch();\n    const json = await response.json();\n    json.isPremium = true;\n    await route.fulfill({ response, json });\n  });\n}\"\n```\n\n### Simulate Network Failures\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.route('**/api/offline', route => route.abort('internetdisconnected'));\n}\"\n# Options: connectionrefused, timedout, connectionreset, internetdisconnected\n```\n\n### Delayed Response\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.route('**/api/slow', async route => {\n    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 3000));\n    route.fulfill({ body: JSON.stringify({ data: 'loaded' }) });\n  });\n}\"\n```\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "running-code.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-client/skill/references/running-code.md",
            "content": "# Running Custom Playwright Code\n\nUse `run-code` to execute arbitrary Playwright code for advanced scenarios not covered by CLI commands.\n\n## Syntax\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  // Your Playwright code here\n  // Access page.context() for browser context operations\n}\"\n```\n\n## Geolocation\n\n```bash\n# Grant geolocation permission and set location\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.context().grantPermissions(['geolocation']);\n  await page.context().setGeolocation({ latitude: 37.7749, longitude: -122.4194 });\n}\"\n\n# Set location to London\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.context().grantPermissions(['geolocation']);\n  await page.context().setGeolocation({ latitude: 51.5074, longitude: -0.1278 });\n}\"\n\n# Clear geolocation override\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.context().clearPermissions();\n}\"\n```\n\n## Permissions\n\n```bash\n# Grant multiple permissions\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.context().grantPermissions([\n    'geolocation',\n    'notifications',\n    'camera',\n    'microphone'\n  ]);\n}\"\n\n# Grant permissions for specific origin\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.context().grantPermissions(['clipboard-read'], {\n    origin: 'https://example.com'\n  });\n}\"\n```\n\n## Media Emulation\n\n```bash\n# Emulate dark color scheme\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' });\n}\"\n\n# Emulate light color scheme\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'light' });\n}\"\n\n# Emulate reduced motion\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });\n}\"\n\n# Emulate print media\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.emulateMedia({ media: 'print' });\n}\"\n```\n\n## Wait Strategies\n\n```bash\n# Wait for network idle\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');\n}\"\n\n# Wait for specific element\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.locator('.loading').waitFor({ state: 'hidden' });\n}\"\n\n# Wait for function to return true\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.appReady === true);\n}\"\n\n# Wait with timeout\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.locator('.result').waitFor({ timeout: 10000 });\n}\"\n```\n\n## Frames and Iframes\n\n```bash\n# Work with iframe\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  const frame = page.locator('iframe#my-iframe').contentFrame();\n  await frame.locator('button').click();\n}\"\n\n# Get all frames\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  const frames = page.frames();\n  return frames.map(f => f.url());\n}\"\n```\n\n## File Downloads\n\n```bash\n# Handle file download\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');\n  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Download' }).click();\n  const download = await downloadPromise;\n  await download.saveAs('./downloaded-file.pdf');\n  return download.suggestedFilename();\n}\"\n```\n\n## Clipboard\n\n```bash\n# Read clipboard (requires permission)\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.context().grantPermissions(['clipboard-read']);\n  return await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.readText());\n}\"\n\n# Write to clipboard\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.evaluate(text => navigator.clipboard.writeText(text), 'Hello clipboard!');\n}\"\n```\n\n## Page Information\n\n```bash\n# Get page title\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  return await page.title();\n}\"\n\n# Get current URL\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  return page.url();\n}\"\n\n# Get page content\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  return await page.content();\n}\"\n\n# Get viewport size\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  return page.viewportSize();\n}\"\n```\n\n## JavaScript Execution\n\n```bash\n# Execute JavaScript and return result\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  return await page.evaluate(() => {\n    return {\n      userAgent: navigator.userAgent,\n      language: navigator.language,\n      cookiesEnabled: navigator.cookieEnabled\n    };\n  });\n}\"\n\n# Pass arguments to evaluate\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  const multiplier = 5;\n  return await page.evaluate(m => document.querySelectorAll('li').length * m, multiplier);\n}\"\n```\n\n## Error Handling\n\n```bash\n# Try-catch in run-code\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  try {\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ timeout: 1000 });\n    return 'clicked';\n  } catch (e) {\n    return 'element not found';\n  }\n}\"\n```\n\n## Complex Workflows\n\n```bash\n# Login and save state\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.goto('https://example.com/login');\n  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' }).fill('user@example.com');\n  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Password' }).fill('secret');\n  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();\n  await page.waitForURL('**/dashboard');\n  await page.context().storageState({ path: 'auth.json' });\n  return 'Login successful';\n}\"\n\n# Scrape data from multiple pages\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  const results = [];\n  for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {\n    await page.goto(\\`https://example.com/page/\\${i}\\`);\n    const items = await page.locator('.item').allTextContents();\n    results.push(...items);\n  }\n  return results;\n}\"\n```\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "session-management.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-client/skill/references/session-management.md",
            "content": "# Browser Session Management\n\nRun multiple isolated browser sessions concurrently with state persistence.\n\n## Named Browser Sessions\n\nUse `-s` flag to isolate browser contexts:\n\n```bash\n# Browser 1: Authentication flow\nplaywright-cli -s=auth open https://app.example.com/login\n\n# Browser 2: Public browsing (separate cookies, storage)\nplaywright-cli -s=public open https://example.com\n\n# Commands are isolated by browser session\nplaywright-cli -s=auth fill e1 \"user@example.com\"\nplaywright-cli -s=public snapshot\n```\n\n## Browser Session Isolation Properties\n\nEach browser session has independent:\n- Cookies\n- LocalStorage / SessionStorage\n- IndexedDB\n- Cache\n- Browsing history\n- Open tabs\n\n## Browser Session Commands\n\n```bash\n# List all browser sessions\nplaywright-cli list\n\n# Stop a browser session (close the browser)\nplaywright-cli close                # stop the default browser\nplaywright-cli -s=mysession close   # stop a named browser\n\n# Stop all browser sessions\nplaywright-cli close-all\n\n# Forcefully kill all daemon processes (for stale/zombie processes)\nplaywright-cli kill-all\n\n# Delete browser session user data (profile directory)\nplaywright-cli delete-data                # delete default browser data\nplaywright-cli -s=mysession delete-data   # delete named browser data\n```\n\n## Environment Variable\n\nSet a default browser session name via environment variable:\n\n```bash\nexport PLAYWRIGHT_CLI_SESSION=\"mysession\"\nplaywright-cli open example.com  # Uses \"mysession\" automatically\n```\n\n## Common Patterns\n\n### Concurrent Scraping\n\n```bash\n#!/bin/bash\n# Scrape multiple sites concurrently\n\n# Start all browsers\nplaywright-cli -s=site1 open https://site1.com &\nplaywright-cli -s=site2 open https://site2.com &\nplaywright-cli -s=site3 open https://site3.com &\nwait\n\n# Take snapshots from each\nplaywright-cli -s=site1 snapshot\nplaywright-cli -s=site2 snapshot\nplaywright-cli -s=site3 snapshot\n\n# Cleanup\nplaywright-cli close-all\n```\n\n### A/B Testing Sessions\n\n```bash\n# Test different user experiences\nplaywright-cli -s=variant-a open \"https://app.com?variant=a\"\nplaywright-cli -s=variant-b open \"https://app.com?variant=b\"\n\n# Compare\nplaywright-cli -s=variant-a screenshot\nplaywright-cli -s=variant-b screenshot\n```\n\n### Persistent Profile\n\nBy default, browser profile is kept in memory only. Use `--persistent` flag on `open` to persist the browser profile to disk:\n\n```bash\n# Use persistent profile (auto-generated location)\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com --persistent\n\n# Use persistent profile with custom directory\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com --profile=/path/to/profile\n```\n\n## Default Browser Session\n\nWhen `-s` is omitted, commands use the default browser session:\n\n```bash\n# These use the same default browser session\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com\nplaywright-cli snapshot\nplaywright-cli close  # Stops default browser\n```\n\n## Browser Session Configuration\n\nConfigure a browser session with specific settings when opening:\n\n```bash\n# Open with config file\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com --config=.playwright/my-cli.json\n\n# Open with specific browser\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com --browser=firefox\n\n# Open in headed mode\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com --headed\n\n# Open with persistent profile\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com --persistent\n```\n\n## Best Practices\n\n### 1. Name Browser Sessions Semantically\n\n```bash\n# GOOD: Clear purpose\nplaywright-cli -s=github-auth open https://github.com\nplaywright-cli -s=docs-scrape open https://docs.example.com\n\n# AVOID: Generic names\nplaywright-cli -s=s1 open https://github.com\n```\n\n### 2. Always Clean Up\n\n```bash\n# Stop browsers when done\nplaywright-cli -s=auth close\nplaywright-cli -s=scrape close\n\n# Or stop all at once\nplaywright-cli close-all\n\n# If browsers become unresponsive or zombie processes remain\nplaywright-cli kill-all\n```\n\n### 3. Delete Stale Browser Data\n\n```bash\n# Remove old browser data to free disk space\nplaywright-cli -s=oldsession delete-data\n```\n"

            "name": "storage-state.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-client/skill/references/storage-state.md",
            "content": "# Storage Management\n\nManage cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, and browser storage state.\n\n## Storage State\n\nSave and restore complete browser state including cookies and storage.\n\n### Save Storage State\n\n```bash\n# Save to auto-generated filename (storage-state-{timestamp}.json)\nplaywright-cli state-save\n\n# Save to specific filename\nplaywright-cli state-save my-auth-state.json\n```\n\n### Restore Storage State\n\n```bash\n# Load storage state from file\nplaywright-cli state-load my-auth-state.json\n\n# Reload page to apply cookies\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com\n```\n\n### Storage State File Format\n\nThe saved file contains:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"cookies\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"session_id\",\n      \"value\": \"abc123\",\n      \"domain\": \"example.com\",\n      \"path\": \"/\",\n      \"expires\": 1735689600,\n      \"httpOnly\": true,\n      \"secure\": true,\n      \"sameSite\": \"Lax\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"origins\": [\n    {\n      \"origin\": \"https://example.com\",\n      \"localStorage\": [\n        { \"name\": \"theme\", \"value\": \"dark\" },\n        { \"name\": \"user_id\", \"value\": \"12345\" }\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Cookies\n\n### List All Cookies\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli cookie-list\n```\n\n### Filter Cookies by Domain\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli cookie-list --domain=example.com\n```\n\n### Filter Cookies by Path\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli cookie-list --path=/api\n```\n\n### Get Specific Cookie\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli cookie-get session_id\n```\n\n### Set a Cookie\n\n```bash\n# Basic cookie\nplaywright-cli cookie-set session abc123\n\n# Cookie with options\nplaywright-cli cookie-set session abc123 --domain=example.com --path=/ --httpOnly --secure --sameSite=Lax\n\n# Cookie with expiration (Unix timestamp)\nplaywright-cli cookie-set remember_me token123 --expires=1735689600\n```\n\n### Delete a Cookie\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli cookie-delete session_id\n```\n\n### Clear All Cookies\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli cookie-clear\n```\n\n### Advanced: Multiple Cookies or Custom Options\n\nFor complex scenarios like adding multiple cookies at once, use `run-code`:\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.context().addCookies([\n    { name: 'session_id', value: 'sess_abc123', domain: 'example.com', path: '/', httpOnly: true },\n    { name: 'preferences', value: JSON.stringify({ theme: 'dark' }), domain: 'example.com', path: '/' }\n  ]);\n}\"\n```\n\n## Local Storage\n\n### List All localStorage Items\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli localstorage-list\n```\n\n### Get Single Value\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli localstorage-get token\n```\n\n### Set Value\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli localstorage-set theme dark\n```\n\n### Set JSON Value\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli localstorage-set user_settings '{\"theme\":\"dark\",\"language\":\"en\"}'\n```\n\n### Delete Single Item\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli localstorage-delete token\n```\n\n### Clear All localStorage\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli localstorage-clear\n```\n\n### Advanced: Multiple Operations\n\nFor complex scenarios like setting multiple values at once, use `run-code`:\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.evaluate(() => {\n    localStorage.setItem('token', 'jwt_abc123');\n    localStorage.setItem('user_id', '12345');\n    localStorage.setItem('expires_at', Date.now() + 3600000);\n  });\n}\"\n```\n\n## Session Storage\n\n### List All sessionStorage Items\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli sessionstorage-list\n```\n\n### Get Single Value\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli sessionstorage-get form_data\n```\n\n### Set Value\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli sessionstorage-set step 3\n```\n\n### Delete Single Item\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli sessionstorage-delete step\n```\n\n### Clear sessionStorage\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli sessionstorage-clear\n```\n\n## IndexedDB\n\n### List Databases\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  return await page.evaluate(async () => {\n    const databases = await indexedDB.databases();\n    return databases;\n  });\n}\"\n```\n\n### Delete Database\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => {\n  await page.evaluate(() => {\n    indexedDB.deleteDatabase('myDatabase');\n  });\n}\"\n```\n\n## Common Patterns\n\n### Authentication State Reuse\n\n```bash\n# Step 1: Login and save state\nplaywright-cli open https://app.example.com/login\nplaywright-cli snapshot\nplaywright-cli fill e1 \"user@example.com\"\nplaywright-cli fill e2 \"password123\"\nplaywright-cli click e3\n\n# Save the authenticated state\nplaywright-cli state-save auth.json\n\n# Step 2: Later, restore state and skip login\nplaywright-cli state-load auth.json\nplaywright-cli open https://app.example.com/dashboard\n# Already logged in!\n```\n\n### Save and Restore Roundtrip\n\n```bash\n# Set up authentication state\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com\nplaywright-cli eval \"() => { document.cookie = 'session=abc123'; localStorage.setItem('user', 'john'); }\"\n\n# Save state to file\nplaywright-cli state-save my-session.json\n\n# ... later, in a new session ...\n\n# Restore state\nplaywright-cli state-load my-session.json\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com\n# Cookies and localStorage are restored!\n```\n\n## Security Notes\n\n- Never commit storage state files containing auth tokens\n- Add `*.auth-state.json` to `.gitignore`\n- Delete state files after automation completes\n- Use environment variables for sensitive data\n- By default, sessions run in-memory mode which is safer for sensitive operations\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "test-generation.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-client/skill/references/test-generation.md",
            "content": "# Test Generation\n\nGenerate Playwright test code automatically as you interact with the browser.\n\n## How It Works\n\nEvery action you perform with `playwright-cli` generates corresponding Playwright TypeScript code.\nThis code appears in the output and can be copied directly into your test files.\n\n## Example Workflow\n\n```bash\n# Start a session\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com/login\n\n# Take a snapshot to see elements\nplaywright-cli snapshot\n# Output shows: e1 [textbox \"Email\"], e2 [textbox \"Password\"], e3 [button \"Sign In\"]\n\n# Fill form fields - generates code automatically\nplaywright-cli fill e1 \"user@example.com\"\n# Ran Playwright code:\n# await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' }).fill('user@example.com');\n\nplaywright-cli fill e2 \"password123\"\n# Ran Playwright code:\n# await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Password' }).fill('password123');\n\nplaywright-cli click e3\n# Ran Playwright code:\n# await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign In' }).click();\n```\n\n## Building a Test File\n\nCollect the generated code into a Playwright test:\n\n```typescript\nimport { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';\n\ntest('login flow', async ({ page }) => {\n  // Generated code from playwright-cli session:\n  await page.goto('https://example.com/login');\n  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' }).fill('user@example.com');\n  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Password' }).fill('password123');\n  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign In' }).click();\n\n  // Add assertions\n  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/.*dashboard/);\n});\n```\n\n## Best Practices\n\n### 1. Use Semantic Locators\n\nThe generated code uses role-based locators when possible, which are more resilient:\n\n```typescript\n// Generated (good - semantic)\nawait page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click();\n\n// Avoid (fragile - CSS selectors)\nawait page.locator('#submit-btn').click();\n```\n\n### 2. Explore Before Recording\n\nTake snapshots to understand the page structure before recording actions:\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com\nplaywright-cli snapshot\n# Review the element structure\nplaywright-cli click e5\n```\n\n### 3. Add Assertions Manually\n\nGenerated code captures actions but not assertions. Add expectations in your test:\n\n```typescript\n// Generated action\nawait page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click();\n\n// Manual assertion\nawait expect(page.getByText('Success')).toBeVisible();\n```\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "tracing.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-client/skill/references/tracing.md",
            "content": "# Tracing\n\nCapture detailed execution traces for debugging and analysis. Traces include DOM snapshots, screenshots, network activity, and console logs.\n\n## Basic Usage\n\n```bash\n# Start trace recording\nplaywright-cli tracing-start\n\n# Perform actions\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com\nplaywright-cli click e1\nplaywright-cli fill e2 \"test\"\n\n# Stop trace recording\nplaywright-cli tracing-stop\n```\n\n## Trace Output Files\n\nWhen you start tracing, Playwright creates a `traces/` directory with several files:\n\n### `trace-{timestamp}.trace`\n\n**Action log** - The main trace file containing:\n- Every action performed (clicks, fills, navigations)\n- DOM snapshots before and after each action\n- Screenshots at each step\n- Timing information\n- Console messages\n- Source locations\n\n### `trace-{timestamp}.network`\n\n**Network log** - Complete network activity:\n- All HTTP requests and responses\n- Request headers and bodies\n- Response headers and bodies\n- Timing (DNS, connect, TLS, TTFB, download)\n- Resource sizes\n- Failed requests and errors\n\n### `resources/`\n\n**Resources directory** - Cached resources:\n- Images, fonts, stylesheets, scripts\n- Response bodies for replay\n- Assets needed to reconstruct page state\n\n## What Traces Capture\n\n| Category | Details |\n|----------|---------|\n| **Actions** | Clicks, fills, hovers, keyboard input, navigations |\n| **DOM** | Full DOM snapshot before/after each action |\n| **Screenshots** | Visual state at each step |\n| **Network** | All requests, responses, headers, bodies, timing |\n| **Console** | All console.log, warn, error messages |\n| **Timing** | Precise timing for each operation |\n\n## Use Cases\n\n### Debugging Failed Actions\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli tracing-start\nplaywright-cli open https://app.example.com\n\n# This click fails - why?\nplaywright-cli click e5\n\nplaywright-cli tracing-stop\n# Open trace to see DOM state when click was attempted\n```\n\n### Analyzing Performance\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli tracing-start\nplaywright-cli open https://slow-site.com\nplaywright-cli tracing-stop\n\n# View network waterfall to identify slow resources\n```\n\n### Capturing Evidence\n\n```bash\n# Record a complete user flow for documentation\nplaywright-cli tracing-start\n\nplaywright-cli open https://app.example.com/checkout\nplaywright-cli fill e1 \"4111111111111111\"\nplaywright-cli fill e2 \"12/25\"\nplaywright-cli fill e3 \"123\"\nplaywright-cli click e4\n\nplaywright-cli tracing-stop\n# Trace shows exact sequence of events\n```\n\n## Trace vs Video vs Screenshot\n\n| Feature | Trace | Video | Screenshot |\n|---------|-------|-------|------------|\n| **Format** | .trace file | .webm video | .png/.jpeg image |\n| **DOM inspection** | Yes | No | No |\n| **Network details** | Yes | No | No |\n| **Step-by-step replay** | Yes | Continuous | Single frame |\n| **File size** | Medium | Large | Small |\n| **Best for** | Debugging | Demos | Quick capture |\n\n## Best Practices\n\n### 1. Start Tracing Before the Problem\n\n```bash\n# Trace the entire flow, not just the failing step\nplaywright-cli tracing-start\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com\n# ... all steps leading to the issue ...\nplaywright-cli tracing-stop\n```\n\n### 2. Clean Up Old Traces\n\nTraces can consume significant disk space:\n\n```bash\n# Remove traces older than 7 days\nfind .playwright-cli/traces -mtime +7 -delete\n```\n\n## Limitations\n\n- Traces add overhead to automation\n- Large traces can consume significant disk space\n- Some dynamic content may not replay perfectly\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "video-recording.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-client/skill/references/video-recording.md",
            "content": "# Video Recording\n\nCapture browser automation sessions as video for debugging, documentation, or verification. Produces WebM (VP8/VP9 codec).\n\n## Basic Recording\n\n```bash\n# Open browser first\nplaywright-cli open\n\n# Start recording\nplaywright-cli video-start demo.webm\n\n# Add a chapter marker for section transitions\nplaywright-cli video-chapter \"Getting Started\" --description=\"Opening the homepage\" --duration=2000\n\n# Navigate and perform actions\nplaywright-cli goto https://example.com\nplaywright-cli snapshot\nplaywright-cli click e1\n\n# Add another chapter\nplaywright-cli video-chapter \"Filling Form\" --description=\"Entering test data\" --duration=2000\nplaywright-cli fill e2 \"test input\"\n\n# Stop and save\nplaywright-cli video-stop\n```\n\n## Best Practices\n\n### 1. Use Descriptive Filenames\n\n```bash\n# Include context in filename\nplaywright-cli video-start recordings/login-flow-2024-01-15.webm\nplaywright-cli video-start recordings/checkout-test-run-42.webm\n```\n\n### 2. Record entire hero scripts.\n\nWhen recording a video for the user or as a proof of work, it is best to create a code snippet and execute it with run-code.\nIt allows pulling appropriate pauses between the actions and annotating the video. There are new Playwright APIs for that.\n\n1) Perform scenario using CLI and take note of all locators and actions. You'll need those locators to request thier bounding boxes for highlight.\n2) Create a file with the intended script for video (below). Use pressSequentially w/ delay for nice typing, make reasonable pauses.\n3) Use playwright-cli run-code --file your-script.js\n\n**Important**: Overlays are `pointer-events: none` \u2014 they do not interfere with page interactions. You can safely keep sticky overlays visible while clicking, filling, or performing any actions on the page.\n\n```js\nasync page => {\n  await page.screencast.start({ path: 'video.webm', size: { width: 1280, height: 800 } });\n  await page.goto('https://demo.playwright.dev/todomvc');\n\n  // Show a chapter card \u2014 blurs the page and shows a dialog.\n  // Blocks until duration expires, then auto-removes.\n  // Use this for simple use cases, but always feel free to hand-craft your own beautiful\n  // overlay via await page.screencast.showOverlay().\n  await page.screencast.showChapter('Adding Todo Items', {\n    description: 'We will add several items to the todo list.',\n    duration: 2000,\n  });\n\n  // Perform action\n  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'What needs to be done?' }).pressSequentially('Walk the dog', { delay: 60 });\n  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'What needs to be done?' }).press('Enter');\n  await page.waitForTimeout(1000);\n\n  // Show next chapter\n  await page.screencast.showChapter('Verifying Results', {\n    description: 'Checking the item appeared in the list.',\n    duration: 2000,\n  });\n\n  // Add a sticky annotation that stays while you perform actions.\n  // Overlays are pointer-events: none, so they won't block clicks.\n  const annotation = await page.screencast.showOverlay(`\n    <div style=\"position: absolute; top: 8px; right: 8px;\n      padding: 6px 12px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.7);\n      border-radius: 8px; font-size: 13px; color: white;\">\n      \u2713 Item added successfully\n    </div>\n  `);\n\n  // Perform more actions while the annotation is visible\n  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'What needs to be done?' }).pressSequentially('Buy groceries', { delay: 60 });\n  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'What needs to be done?' }).press('Enter');\n  await page.waitForTimeout(1500);\n\n  // Remove the annotation when done\n  await annotation.dispose();\n\n  // You can also highlight relevant locators and provide contextual annotations.\n  const bounds = await page.getByText('Walk the dog').boundingBox();\n  await page.screencast.showOverlay(`\n    <div style=\"position: absolute;\n      top: ${bounds.y}px;\n      left: ${bounds.x}px;\n      width: ${bounds.width}px;\n      height: ${bounds.height}px;\n      border: 1px solid red;\">\n    </div>\n    <div style=\"position: absolute;\n      top: ${bounds.y + bounds.height + 5}px;\n      left: ${bounds.x + bounds.width / 2}px;\n      transform: translateX(-50%);\n      padding: 6px;\n      background: #808080;\n      border-radius: 10px;\n      font-size: 14px;\n      color: white;\">Check it out, it is right above this text\n    </div>\n  `, { duration: 2000 });\n\n  await page.screencast.stop();\n}\n```\n\nEmbrace creativity, overlays are powerful.\n\n### Overlay API Summary\n\n| Method | Use Case |\n|--------|----------|\n| `page.screencast.showChapter(title, { description?, duration?, styleSheet? })` | Full-screen chapter card with blurred backdrop \u2014 ideal for section transitions |\n| `page.screencast.showOverlay(html, { duration? })` | Custom HTML overlay \u2014 use for callouts, labels, highlights |\n| `disposable.dispose()` | Remove a sticky overlay added without duration |\n| `page.screencast.hideOverlays()` / `page.screencast.showOverlays()` | Temporarily hide/show all overlays |\n\n## Tracing vs Video\n\n| Feature | Video | Tracing |\n|---------|-------|---------|\n| Output | WebM file | Trace file (viewable in Trace Viewer) |\n| Shows | Visual recording | DOM snapshots, network, console, actions |\n| Use case | Demos, documentation | Debugging, analysis |\n| Size | Larger | Smaller |\n\n## Limitations\n\n- Recording adds slight overhead to automation\n- Large recordings can consume significant disk space\n"
          },
          {
            "name": "SKILL.md",
            "path": "workspace/demo-clients/northstar-media-lab/presentation/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.59.1/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-client/skill/SKILL.md",
            "content": "---\nname: playwright-cli\ndescription: Automate browser interactions, test web pages and work with Playwright tests.\nallowed-tools: Bash(playwright-cli:*) Bash(npx:*) Bash(npm:*)\n---\n\n# Browser Automation with playwright-cli\n\n## Quick start\n\n```bash\n# open new browser\nplaywright-cli open\n# navigate to a page\nplaywright-cli goto https://playwright.dev\n# interact with the page using refs from the snapshot\nplaywright-cli click e15\nplaywright-cli type \"page.click\"\nplaywright-cli press Enter\n# take a screenshot (rarely used, as snapshot is more common)\nplaywright-cli screenshot\n# close the browser\nplaywright-cli close\n```\n\n## Commands\n\n### Core\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli open\n# open and navigate right away\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com/\nplaywright-cli goto https://playwright.dev\nplaywright-cli type \"search query\"\nplaywright-cli click e3\nplaywright-cli dblclick e7\n# --submit presses Enter after filling the element\nplaywright-cli fill e5 \"user@example.com\"  --submit\nplaywright-cli drag e2 e8\nplaywright-cli hover e4\nplaywright-cli select e9 \"option-value\"\nplaywright-cli upload ./document.pdf\nplaywright-cli check e12\nplaywright-cli uncheck e12\nplaywright-cli snapshot\nplaywright-cli eval \"document.title\"\nplaywright-cli eval \"el => el.textContent\" e5\n# get element id, class, or any attribute not visible in the snapshot\nplaywright-cli eval \"el => el.id\" e5\nplaywright-cli eval \"el => el.getAttribute('data-testid')\" e5\nplaywright-cli dialog-accept\nplaywright-cli dialog-accept \"confirmation text\"\nplaywright-cli dialog-dismiss\nplaywright-cli resize 1920 1080\nplaywright-cli close\n```\n\n### Navigation\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli go-back\nplaywright-cli go-forward\nplaywright-cli reload\n```\n\n### Keyboard\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli press Enter\nplaywright-cli press ArrowDown\nplaywright-cli keydown Shift\nplaywright-cli keyup Shift\n```\n\n### Mouse\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli mousemove 150 300\nplaywright-cli mousedown\nplaywright-cli mousedown right\nplaywright-cli mouseup\nplaywright-cli mouseup right\nplaywright-cli mousewheel 0 100\n```\n\n### Save as\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli screenshot\nplaywright-cli screenshot e5\nplaywright-cli screenshot --filename=page.png\nplaywright-cli pdf --filename=page.pdf\n```\n\n### Tabs\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli tab-list\nplaywright-cli tab-new\nplaywright-cli tab-new https://example.com/page\nplaywright-cli tab-close\nplaywright-cli tab-close 2\nplaywright-cli tab-select 0\n```\n\n### Storage\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli state-save\nplaywright-cli state-save auth.json\nplaywright-cli state-load auth.json\n\n# Cookies\nplaywright-cli cookie-list\nplaywright-cli cookie-list --domain=example.com\nplaywright-cli cookie-get session_id\nplaywright-cli cookie-set session_id abc123\nplaywright-cli cookie-set session_id abc123 --domain=example.com --httpOnly --secure\nplaywright-cli cookie-delete session_id\nplaywright-cli cookie-clear\n\n# LocalStorage\nplaywright-cli localstorage-list\nplaywright-cli localstorage-get theme\nplaywright-cli localstorage-set theme dark\nplaywright-cli localstorage-delete theme\nplaywright-cli localstorage-clear\n\n# SessionStorage\nplaywright-cli sessionstorage-list\nplaywright-cli sessionstorage-get step\nplaywright-cli sessionstorage-set step 3\nplaywright-cli sessionstorage-delete step\nplaywright-cli sessionstorage-clear\n```\n\n### Network\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli route \"**/*.jpg\" --status=404\nplaywright-cli route \"https://api.example.com/**\" --body='{\"mock\": true}'\nplaywright-cli route-list\nplaywright-cli unroute \"**/*.jpg\"\nplaywright-cli unroute\n```\n\n### DevTools\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli console\nplaywright-cli console warning\nplaywright-cli network\nplaywright-cli run-code \"async page => await page.context().grantPermissions(['geolocation'])\"\nplaywright-cli run-code --filename=script.js\nplaywright-cli tracing-start\nplaywright-cli tracing-stop\nplaywright-cli video-start video.webm\nplaywright-cli video-chapter \"Chapter Title\" --description=\"Details\" --duration=2000\nplaywright-cli video-stop\n```\n\n## Open parameters\n```bash\n# Use specific browser when creating session\nplaywright-cli open --browser=chrome\nplaywright-cli open --browser=firefox\nplaywright-cli open --browser=webkit\nplaywright-cli open --browser=msedge\n# Connect to browser via extension\nplaywright-cli open --extension\n\n# Use persistent profile (by default profile is in-memory)\nplaywright-cli open --persistent\n# Use persistent profile with custom directory\nplaywright-cli open --profile=/path/to/profile\n\n# Start with config file\nplaywright-cli open --config=my-config.json\n\n# Close the browser\nplaywright-cli close\n# Delete user data for the default session\nplaywright-cli delete-data\n```\n\n## Snapshots\n\nAfter each command, playwright-cli provides a snapshot of the current browser state.\n\n```bash\n> playwright-cli goto https://example.com\n### Page\n- Page URL: https://example.com/\n- Page Title: Example Domain\n### Snapshot\n[Snapshot](.playwright-cli/page-2026-02-14T19-22-42-679Z.yml)\n```\n\nYou can also take a snapshot on demand using `playwright-cli snapshot` command. All the options below can be combined as needed.\n\n```bash\n# default - save to a file with timestamp-based name\nplaywright-cli snapshot\n\n# save to file, use when snapshot is a part of the workflow result\nplaywright-cli snapshot --filename=after-click.yaml\n\n# snapshot an element instead of the whole page\nplaywright-cli snapshot \"#main\"\n\n# limit snapshot depth for efficiency, take a partial snapshot afterwards\nplaywright-cli snapshot --depth=4\nplaywright-cli snapshot e34\n```\n\n## Targeting elements\n\nBy default, use refs from the snapshot to interact with page elements.\n\n```bash\n# get snapshot with refs\nplaywright-cli snapshot\n\n# interact using a ref\nplaywright-cli click e15\n```\n\nYou can also use css selectors or Playwright locators.\n\n```bash\n# css selector\nplaywright-cli click \"#main > button.submit\"\n\n# role locator\nplaywright-cli click \"getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })\"\n\n# test id\nplaywright-cli click \"getByTestId('submit-button')\"\n```\n\n## Browser Sessions\n\n```bash\n# create new browser session named \"mysession\" with persistent profile\nplaywright-cli -s=mysession open example.com --persistent\n# same with manually specified profile directory (use when requested explicitly)\nplaywright-cli -s=mysession open example.com --profile=/path/to/profile\nplaywright-cli -s=mysession click e6\nplaywright-cli -s=mysession close  # stop a named browser\nplaywright-cli -s=mysession delete-data  # delete user data for persistent session\n\nplaywright-cli list\n# Close all browsers\nplaywright-cli close-all\n# Forcefully kill all browser processes\nplaywright-cli kill-all\n```\n\n## Installation\n\nIf global `playwright-cli` command is not available, try a local version via `npx playwright-cli`:\n\n```bash\nnpx --no-install playwright-cli --version\n```\n\nWhen local version is available, use `npx playwright-cli` in all commands. Otherwise, install `playwright-cli` as a global command:\n\n```bash\nnpm install -g @playwright/cli@latest\n```\n\n## Example: Form submission\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com/form\nplaywright-cli snapshot\n\nplaywright-cli fill e1 \"user@example.com\"\nplaywright-cli fill e2 \"password123\"\nplaywright-cli click e3\nplaywright-cli snapshot\nplaywright-cli close\n```\n\n## Example: Multi-tab workflow\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com\nplaywright-cli tab-new https://example.com/other\nplaywright-cli tab-list\nplaywright-cli tab-select 0\nplaywright-cli snapshot\nplaywright-cli close\n```\n\n## Example: Debugging with DevTools\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com\nplaywright-cli click e4\nplaywright-cli fill e7 \"test\"\nplaywright-cli console\nplaywright-cli network\nplaywright-cli close\n```\n\n```bash\nplaywright-cli open https://example.com\nplaywright-cli tracing-start\nplaywright-cli click e4\nplaywright-cli fill e7 \"test\"\nplaywright-cli tracing-stop\nplaywright-cli close\n```\n\n## Specific tasks\n\n* **Running and Debugging Playwright tests** [references/playwright-tests.md](references/playwright-tests.md)\n* **Request mocking** [references/request-mocking.md](references/request-mocking.md)\n* **Running Playwright code** [references/running-code.md](references/running-code.md)\n* **Browser session management** [references/session-management.md](references/session-management.md)\n* **Storage state (cookies, localStorage)** [references/storage-state.md](references/storage-state.md)\n* **Test generation** [references/test-generation.md](references/test-generation.md)\n* **Tracing** [references/tracing.md](references/tracing.md)\n* **Video recording** [references/video-recording.md](references/video-recording.md)\n* **Inspecting element attributes** [references/element-attributes.md](references/element-attributes.md)\n"

            "name": "SKILL.md",

            "content": "---\nname: playwright-trace\ndescription: Inspect Playwright trace files from the command line \u2014 list actions, view requests, console, errors, snapshots and screenshots.\nallowed-tools: Bash(npx:*)\n---\n\n# Playwright Trace CLI\n\nInspect `.zip` trace files produced by Playwright tests without opening a browser.\n\n## Workflow\n\n1. Start with `trace open <trace.zip>` to extract the trace and see its metadata.\n2. Use `trace actions` to see all actions with their action IDs.\n3. Use `trace action <action-id>` to drill into a specific action \u2014 see parameters, logs, source location, and available snapshots.\n4. Use `trace requests`, `trace console`, or `trace errors` for cross-cutting views.\n5. Use `trace snapshot <action-id>` to get the DOM snapshot, or run a browser command against it.\n6. Use `trace close` to remove the extracted trace data when done.\n\nAll commands after `open` operate on the currently opened trace \u2014 no need to pass the trace file again. Opening a new trace replaces the previous one.\n\n## Commands\n\n### Open a trace\n\n```bash\n# Extract trace and show metadata: browser, viewport, duration, action/error counts\nnpx playwright trace open <trace.zip>\n```\n\n### Close a trace\n\n```bash\n# Remove extracted trace data\nnpx playwright trace close\n```\n\n### Actions\n\n```bash\n# List all actions as a tree with action IDs and timing\nnpx playwright trace actions\n\n# Filter by action title (regex, case-insensitive)\nnpx playwright trace actions --grep \"click\"\n\n# Only failed actions\nnpx playwright trace actions --errors-only\n```\n\n### Action details\n\n```bash\n# Show full details for one action: params, result, logs, source, snapshots\nnpx playwright trace action <action-id>\n```\n\nThe `action` command displays available snapshot phases (before, input, after) and the exact command to extract them.\n\n### Requests\n\n```bash\n# All network requests: method, status, URL, duration, size\nnpx playwright trace requests\n\n# Filter by URL pattern\nnpx playwright trace requests --grep \"api\"\n\n# Filter by HTTP method\nnpx playwright trace requests --method POST\n\n# Only failed requests (status >= 400)\nnpx playwright trace requests --failed\n```\n\n### Request details\n\n```bash\n# Show full details for one request: headers, body, security\nnpx playwright trace request <request-id>\n```\n\n### Console\n\n```bash\n# All console messages and stdout/stderr\nnpx playwright trace console\n\n# Only errors\nnpx playwright trace console --errors-only\n\n# Only browser console (no stdout/stderr)\nnpx playwright trace console --browser\n\n# Only stdout/stderr (no browser console)\nnpx playwright trace console --stdio\n```\n\n### Errors\n\n```bash\n# All errors with stack traces and associated actions\nnpx playwright trace errors\n```\n\n### Snapshots\n\nThe `snapshot` command loads the DOM snapshot for an action into a headless browser and runs a single browser command against it. Without a browser command, it returns the accessibility snapshot.\n\n```bash\n# Get the accessibility snapshot (default)\nnpx playwright trace snapshot <action-id>\n\n# Use a specific phase\nnpx playwright trace snapshot <action-id> --name before\n\n# Run eval to query the DOM\nnpx playwright trace snapshot <action-id> -- eval \"document.title\"\nnpx playwright trace snapshot <action-id> -- eval \"document.querySelector('#error').textContent\"\n\n# Eval on a specific element ref (from the snapshot)\nnpx playwright trace snapshot <action-id> -- eval \"el => el.getAttribute('data-testid')\" e5\n\n# Take a screenshot of the snapshot\nnpx playwright trace snapshot <action-id> -- screenshot\n\n# Redirect output to a file\nnpx playwright trace snapshot <action-id> -- eval \"document.body.outerHTML\" --filename=page.html\nnpx playwright trace snapshot <action-id> -- screenshot --filename=screenshot.png\n```\n\nOnly three browser commands are useful on a frozen snapshot: `snapshot`, `eval`, and `screenshot`.\n\n### Attachments\n\n```bash\n# List all trace attachments\nnpx playwright trace attachments\n\n# Extract an attachment by its number\nnpx playwright trace attachment 1\nnpx playwright trace attachment 1 -o out.png\n```\n\n## Typical investigation\n\n```bash\n# 1. Open the trace and see what's inside\nnpx playwright trace open test-results/my-test/trace.zip\n\n# 2. What actions ran?\nnpx playwright trace actions\n\n# 3. Which action failed?\nnpx playwright trace actions --errors-only\n\n# 4. What went wrong?\nnpx playwright trace action 12\n\n# 5. What did the page look like at that moment?\nnpx playwright trace snapshot 12\n\n# 6. Query the DOM for more detail\nnpx playwright trace snapshot 12 -- eval \"document.querySelector('.error-message').textContent\"\n\n# 7. Any relevant network failures?\nnpx playwright trace requests --failed\n\n# 8. Any console errors?\nnpx playwright trace console --errors-only\n```\n"
          },
